authorisation: The Product Owner's request of 2026-10-28: remove unwanted and unneeded documents (plans already done, old documents), update any document that does not reflect the current state, and remove every merged branch.
context: Six deliveries (#256-#261) merged on 2026-10-27/28 left 128 merged branches on GitHub and locally, a hundred stale local PR refs, and finished per-delivery documents.
changes: Branches: every merged branch deleted on GitHub (28) and locally (217), plus 100 stale local refs/remotes/pr/* (old PR heads, never on GitHub); only master remains. Nothing unmerged was lost: the one local branch with unique commits (fix/guest-network-untagged-parent, the bridge-RUNNING wait) is in master as waitBridgesRunning, and the redaction backup branch was the Product Owner's to drop. Documents: 40 per-delivery change manifests no tool or record reads, and six superseded status documents (PHASE19_ASSESSMENT, PHASE19_FINAL_REPORT, CURRENT_STATE_ASSESSMENT, COMMERCIAL_ONBOARDING_EXECUTION_STATUS, CONTROL_PLANE_MIGRATION, SYNC_PROTOCOL), all in git history; live links to them rewritten, historical records that mention them untouched. README.md, docs/README.md and CONTINUATION.md rewritten to the current state.
kept_on_purpose: Every document a validator, the pack builder or a governance record reads (records must not be falsified, CLAUDE.md 0D), the Phase*-change-manifest files tools/project-state.py globs, and the backend and performance audits, which are open backlogs.
verification: Reference map over every tracked document (tooling, CI, governance, other documents) before deleting; no broken relative link in the entry documents; validate-standing-records, project-state validate and check-generated pass; build-packs passes; transition-time, state-parity, delivery-protocol and migration-location validators pass. GitHub: only refs/heads/master; no open pull request.
follow_up: Many reference documents (user guides, the operations manual, SYSTEM_OVERVIEW as a marked historical snapshot) were not rewritten line by line; the system handbook and the installation manual are the current references.
